declares them and answers k/n per roster. Same two columns as the facets
before it — the decls the weave carries, the refs column — restricted to

half, never its consumer. So k/n reads as how much of a surface is actually
reached, which is what all three finds were asking.

mentl/a25b99c:
Plan box H.4 per docs/specs/simulations/PLAN-to-first-light.md §3.

The phase concatenates the wheel in canonical order (find src -name
'*.nx' | sort + find lib -name '*.nx' | sort, matching CLAUDE.md
operational essentials), runs pass-2 (seed → inka2.wat) and pass-3
(inka2.wasm → inka3.wat), then diffs. Empirical state surfaces as
visible-progress metrics: function count, line count, NFre count.

Branch logic: if pass-2 produces only seed scaffolding (≤ 2 funcs),
the harness reports 'L1 not yet ready' and exits success on the
existing WABT-gate checks. When sufficient wheel-fn surface emerges
(Phase H closures land), the branch falls through to wat2wasm +
wasm-validate the pass-2 WAT, then runs pass-3 against pass-2.wasm
applied to the same wheel input, then byte-diffs pass-2 vs pass-3.
Identical = L1 closed; diff = exit 1 with diff-size diagnostic.

Current cursor: pass-2 emits 2 funcs, 12 NFre. Phase H handles
(H.1.b/c, H.2.a/c/e, H.3.b done, H.3.c remaining + ad-hoc empirical

mentl/a2edd50:
Makes the f87abf3 oracle keystone substrate functional. Without
this edit, mentl_oracle.nx's cached_check_with_oracle handler had
nothing to subscribe to — graph_mutated was declared (types.nx:641
Mutate effect) but no handler emitted it.

Substrate edits:

1. Add `checkpoint_stack = []` to graph_handler state. Tracks active
   speculation depth — each graph_push_checkpoint pushes the current
   trail_len; each graph_rollback pops. When the stack is empty,
   writes are at the OUTERMOST commit boundary; when non-empty, the
   graph is inside Mentl's speculative loop (or any other
   speculation).

2. graph_push_checkpoint pushes onto checkpoint_stack (resume value
   unchanged; just adds to the with-state).

3. graph_rollback pops checkpoint_stack via slice(stack, 0, n-1).
   Defensive: if stack already empty (anomalous double-rollback), no-op.

4. Each write arm (graph_fresh_ty, graph_fresh_row, graph_bind in
   the success branch, graph_bind_row) checks `len(checkpoint_stack)
   == 0` and performs `graph_mutated(epoch, mutation)` when true.
   Speculative writes (Mentl's exploration between push+rollback)
   leave stack non-empty and never emit — otherwise infinite
   recursion (Mentl would subscribe to her own speculations and
   re-explore forever per the substrate guard documented in
   src/mentl_oracle.nx + INSIGHTS §"The Continuous Oracle IS
   Incremental Compilation Plus One Cached Value").

5. graph_bind / graph_bind_row capture the new_epoch (epoch + 1) into
   a let so the perform reports the post-bump epoch — subscribers
   see the epoch at which the mutation committed.

Eight interrogations:

  Graph         — graph_handler IS the graph; the new event is
                  emitted FROM the graph layer to subscribers above
  Handler       — graph_handler now performs Mutate's graph_mutated
                  op; outer handler (cached_check_with_oracle) catches
  Verb          — N/A at handler-arm level
  Row           — graph_handler's row gains Mutate; w
mentl/a278ecd:
The i32 heuristic (load_i32 >= 1024 → list) fails for strings because
4 packed ASCII bytes always exceed 1024. Restored the 4-byte individual
byte check — works for most cases where list element pointers have null
high bytes (addresses < 64KB). Fails for list elements at high addresses.

The fundamental issue: val_concat cannot distinguish lists of string
pointers from strings when pointer addresses have 4 consecutive printable
ASCII bytes. The correct fix requires full type propagation through
infer_concat_type for all ++ sites — 74 remaining val_concat calls.
